name: Dreamcard V: The Rising Sun

date.source: The card itself promises it “no later than April 25th”, and the FWF's own match report of 17 April 1992 carries it as “coming (for sure) next Wednesday, April 22” (promotions/fwf-1992/archive/fwf-wildfire-vs-cruncher-1992-04-17.html). No results post for the card survives; the FWF's own ledger records the outcome of its own match on it.

appearances.note: Billed defending the RSPWF World Heavyweight Championship against Jushin “Thunder” Liger.
Billed challenging Ric Flair for the RSPWF World Heavyweight Championship.
Billed defending the RSPWF World Jobber Championship against Steve Armstrong.
Billed challenging Ronnie Garvin for the RSPWF World Jobber Championship.
Billed against Sting, a “mega-face vs. mega-face” pairing.
Billed against Hulk Hogan, a “mega-face vs. mega-face” pairing.
Billed “newly returned to American wrestling” against the Great Muta.
Billed against the Ultimate Warrior, billed as “newly returned to American wrestling.”
Billed against Curt Hennig in a Squeegie match — the two men tied at the wrists, a squeegie suspended from the rope's own midpoint for use as a weapon by either man.
Billed against Lex Luger in a Squeegie match — the two men tied at the wrists, a squeegie suspended from the rope's own midpoint for use as a weapon by either man.

Billed against Brian Pillman in a “fastest squash match,” each man set against the Iron Mustafa and the “Mighty” Hercules — neither minted — to see who could squash both opponents in the shorter total time.

Billed against Sid Justice in a “fastest squash match,” each man set against the Iron Mustafa and the “Mighty” Hercules — neither minted — to see who could squash both opponents in the shorter total time.
Billed against Big Van Vader; no stipulation given.
Billed against the Undertaker; no stipulation given.
With the Magician (no other held document names him; left unminted, consistent with the EMWA wing's own treatment of the same billing).

no_appearances_reason: The Bandwidth Championship undercard (one of the newsgroup’s own regulars under a joke persona, another of the newsgroup’s own regulars under a joke persona, one of the newsgroup’s own regulars under a joke persona, a newsgroup regular) is billed on “the newsgroup's own regulars,” per the wing's own roster policy — full first-and-last names that read as plausibly real off-newsgroup identities rather than invented ring personas (the RSPW FAQ's own retrospective account of the Dreamcard series names two of its own maintainers (under personas) as recurring “main event” wrestlers across several cards, unredacted there alongside the plainly fictional “Fluffy the Wonder Bunny,” which cuts both ways and does not resolve the question). Left unminted here on the privacy-first side of that ambiguity rather than guessed either way; see this wing's own digest. The squash match's own jobber opponents, “the Iron Mustafa” and the “Mighty” Hercules, do not resolve confidently to any known real wrestler by those names and are left unminted for the same reason a gap is honestly registered rather than extrapolated.
notes: The FWF's own singles ledger records one result from this card — Doctor Death beating the EMWA World Champion John Girder by disqualification, match 42 (promotions/fwf-1992/archive/fwf-singles-record-1993-01-08.html), now structured above as this show's own matches[] entry. The card was posted twice, on 13 and 16 April 1992; both posts are served, and the fuller of the two (16 April) is this row's own page and the source used to resolve two stipulations the earlier post mislabelled between the same two pairings — the 13 April post attaches “Squeegie match!” to Sid Justice/Pillman with no description, while the fuller 16 April post gives Luger/Hennig the Squeegie stipulation (with its full description) and Sid Justice/Pillman the “fastest squash match” instead; the later, fuller post is treated as the corrected account. Separately, the RSPW newsgroup's own FAQ (1 November 1992, promotions/rspw/archive/faq-for-rec-sport-pro-wrestling-1992-11-01.html) gives a different, uncorroborated account of “Dreamcard V” — subtitled “The Great White North” there rather than “The Rising Sun,” with its main event given as a “Rematch of Sean a maintainers’ joke bout” rather than the Flair/Liger Heavyweight title match this card's own contemporaneous text carries as its Part I headline (this card's own text calls the Bandwidth Championship, not the Heavyweight title match, “the main event for Part I”). The two accounts are not reconciled here — the FAQ is a retrospective summary of six cards compiled six months after the fact by a different poster, and the served Dreamcard V documents are Dreamcard's own contemporaneous primary source — recorded per CURATION.md §7's when-sources-disagree convention rather than silently preferring one.

matches.note: EMWA World Heavyweight Championship (Girder) vs. FWF World Heavyweight Championship (Doctor Death) — an exhibition unification billed as “World Champion vs. World Champion! Title for title!”; neither belt is Dreamcard's own house lineage, so neither is registered as a reign on this card. Doctor Death wins by disqualification, per the FWF's own singles ledger (match 42, promotions/fwf-1992/archive/fwf-singles-record-1993-01-08.html) — Dreamcard's own two posts bill the match but never post a result of their own. The fed's own ledger has Death engineering the finish by throwing Girder a set of brass knuckles and “playing the victim.” An earlier post (dreamcard-v-lineup-update-1992-04-13.html) billed the FWF side as a still-undecided pick between Titan Morgan and Doctor Death (“the winner of the match between Titan Morgan and Doctor Death will represent the FWF”); only Doctor Death appears at Dreamcard V itself, so Titan Morgan carries no appearance on this show.
